A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and analyses of ACSIncome and ACSPublicCoverage, including predictive performance, calibration, selection-bias experiments, and controlled evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and additionally reports absolute subgroup and weighted performance estimates for the ACS tasks.

M1.justification: The causal framework, weighting construction, and subgroup comparison statistic remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 document oracle-weight and cross-fitting procedures already described in v1; they do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven primary simulation settings, three selection mechanisms, and two ACS tasks with the same race/ethnicity subgroups. The additional ACS plots do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Both retain subgroup-agnostic, subgroup-aware, and subgroup-stratified prediction, together with Cai et al.'s shared-space weighting comparison in Figures B18–B24. Newly cited fairness methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 retain the simulation sample sizes, training/test allocation, five-fold model selection, gradient-boosting hyperparameter grid, classification thresholds, and ACS processing. The revised plots do not establish any change to these protocols.

E4.justification: Figure B3 revises the empirical calibration curves examining generalization under selection depending on X, Y, or both Y and A. This updates an existing selection-bias diagnostic while retaining its scenarios and qualitative conclusions; no new ablation or robustness scenario is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10,000 percentile-bootstrap samples, fixed estimated weights during resampling, and Wilson-score intervals for calibration curves. Changed interval endpoints and additional plots using the same uncertainty reporting belong to results changes.

E6.justification: New Figures B34–B40 report absolute subgroup and weighted ACS performance across seven existing metrics. Figure B3's calibration estimates change, and ACS confidence-interval endpoints in B25 and B27–B33 are revised while their point estimates remain unchanged. The principal reported findings are retained.

T1.justification: The conditional-independence results, subgroup-separability argument, and selection-bias derivations in Appendix A.2 remain substantively unchanged. Explicit normalization of the weights and the expanded distribution description clarify the existing construction; Table B3 interprets existing implications rather than introducing a new proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about misleading performance parity and the value of causal reasoning remain intact. The revised introduction adds explicit claims that performance disparities cannot reliably identify where more data or model scaling would help, and that enforcing parity can cause harm without achieving contextually meaningful fairness.

C2.justification: New Table B3 substantially expands practical guidance by distinguishing what test outcomes imply under different controls, predictor inputs, and optimality assumptions. The discussion adds specific limitations concerning continuous or multiclass outcomes, untestable Bayes-optimality, and estimation error in the weight model, alongside a semiparametric direction for future work.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 add implementation-oriented pseudocode for normalized weighted means and held-out weight estimation through cross-fitting. Existing software versions, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and the experiment-code link are retained; relocation of that link does not change access.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references, including Barda et al. on subgroup calibration, Agarwal et al. on fair classification, Kennedy on semiparametric estimation, and work on social welfare and downstream impacts. These extend the context without replacing the paper's causal and distribution-shift positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, causal explanations, and discussion are extensively rewritten. The former Section 3 is reorganized into separate causal-framework and controlled-evaluation sections, subgroup separability moves earlier, and clinical examples and section roadmaps expand the narrative. An acknowledgments section is also added.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table B3 and seven multipanel ACS figures, moves the original main-text Table 2 to Appendix B, and reformats many plots with new markers, legends, and explicit statistic labels. Calibration figures are resized, and Figure B3's erroneous selection label is corrected from A to S.

improvement.justification: Algorithms 1–2, Table B3, and the expanded limitations make the existing framework easier to implement and interpret. Figures B34–B40 improve transparency about the retained ACS results. These provide a useful overall gain in documentation and clarity, although the underlying validation is largely unchanged and some calibration plots become smaller.
